plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: A fragrant evergreen shrub with silvery-gray foliage and slender spikes of small tubular flowers. It is widely grown in gardens and commercial fields, and its blooms attract bees and butterflies in large numbers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June through August in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Mediterranean region; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Tasmania, and the northern United States
plants.funFact: Lavender oil has been used since Roman times, and the plant's name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', because the Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Hydrangea macrophylla
plants.description: A deciduous shrub with large rounded clusters of showy flowers above broad, glossy green leaves. It thrives in partial shade and moist, rich soil, and is a classic feature of summer gardens.
plants.location: Native to Japan; widely cultivated in Europe, the Azores, and eastern North America
plants.funFact: The flower color depends on soil pH and aluminum availability: acidic soils produce blue flowers, while alkaline soils produce pink ones.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with large, round leaves held above the water and spectacular flowers on tall stalks. The leaves have a waxy surface that repels water and dirt. It flowers in warm shallow ponds and wetlands.
plants.location: Asia, from India and China to Japan; also naturalized in northern Australia and parts of the southern United States
plants.funFact: Lotus flowers can regulate their own temperature, staying at about 30–35°C (86–95°F) even when the air is much cooler, which helps attract pollinating beetles.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall subtropical tree with fern-like leaves that is covered with clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender flowers. In some regions it blooms in the southern spring, but in the Northern Hemisphere it also blooms around late spring to early summer in warm climates such as California and Florida.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late May to June in the Northern Hemisphere; October to November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America; planted in Pretoria (South Africa), Sydney, Los Angeles, and Mediterranean-climate cities
plants.funFact: Pretoria is nicknamed the 'Jacaranda City' because tens of thousands of these trees line its streets and carpet the ground with fallen purple blossoms.
